module_title: Vijayanagara and Bahmani Kingdoms - Foundation and Key Rulers
introduction: During the 14th century, as the Delhi Sultanate (under Muhammad Bin Tughlaq) weakened, two major empires emerged in South India. The Hindu empire of 'Vijayanagara' was established south of the Krishna river, and the Islamic 'Bahmani Kingdom' to its north. Both engaged in a continuous struggle over the fertile Raichur Doab region.

core_concepts.title: Foundation of Vijayanagara Empire
core_concepts.description: In 1336 CE, two brothers, 'Harihara and Bukka', established the Vijayanagara (Hampi) empire with the blessings of the sage Vidyaranya.

core_concepts.title: Four Dynasties of Vijayanagara
core_concepts.description: The Vijayanagara Empire was primarily ruled by four dynasties in chronological order: Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu.

core_concepts.title: Krishnadevaraya (Tuluva Dynasty)
core_concepts.description: He was the greatest ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire. The Mughal emperor Babur mentioned him in his autobiography (Baburnama) as the most powerful ruler of India at the time.

core_concepts.title: Foundation of Bahmani Kingdom
core_concepts.description: In 1347 CE, Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (also known as 'Hasan Gangu') founded the Bahmani Kingdom and made Gulbarga its capital.

core_concepts.title: Battle of Talikota (1565 CE)
core_concepts.description: Also known as the Battle of Rakshasi-Tangadi or Bannihatti. A confederacy of Deccan Muslim Sultanates defeated Vijayanagara, leading to the utter destruction of its capital.

important_entities.name: Harihara and Bukka
important_entities.significance: Freed South India from Muslim political dominance and laid the foundation of the Vijayanagara Empire.

important_entities.name: Hasan Gangu (Alauddin Hasan)
important_entities.significance: Established the first independent Islamic state in the Deccan region.

important_entities.name: Krishnadevaraya
important_entities.significance: A great conqueror, patron of literature, and ruler who assumed the title of 'Andhra Bhoja'.

important_entities.name: Raichur Doab
important_entities.key_fact: Land between Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers
important_entities.significance: The primary bone of contention and cause of 200 years of warfare between the Vijayanagara and Bahmani kingdoms.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often mistakenly select 'Krishnadevaraya' as the founder of Vijayanagara because he is the most famous. The correct answer is 'Harihara and Bukka'.
The majestic capital of Vijayanagara is identified today by the extensive ruins at 'Hampi' in Karnataka, located on the banks of the Tungabhadra River.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember the acronym SSTA to recall the exact chronological order of the ruling dynasties.
Both Vijayanagara (1336) and Bahmani (1347) were founded during the reign of Delhi Sultan Muhammad Bin Tughlaq, just 11 years apart.

exam_strategy_tips: Always remember the specific dynasty to which Krishnadevaraya belonged (Tuluva).
The year (1565) and the result of the Battle of Talikota are highly recurring questions in foundational exams.
